mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Cobot Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The TRFCobot Dual has a reference list price of US$ 120,000, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. Installation, line integration, gripper and conveyor interface are quoted with your application, because line speed, case weight, pallet pattern and layout change the scope. Use the payback calculator on this page to estimate what manual palletizing costs you today.

mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. These are typical ranges for commercial screening: TRF confirms the final rate for your product, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Product?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the case weight plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multi-case picks, the combined weight of the cases. TRFCobot handles cases up to about 22 lb, TRFCompact up to about 44 lb and TRFSpeed up to about 66 lb. TRF validates the final payload with your product, gripper, pallet pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: Can a Cobot Palletizer Handle Multiple SKUs and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFCobot supports multiple recipes, pallet patterns and SKU changes without the complexity of a large custom system, which is why it fits co-packers, contract manufacturers and plants with short runs. Each recipe stores the case data and the pallet pattern for one product, and the end-of-arm tool and reach are validated for every case size in your mix.

mainEntity.name: What Floor Space and Reach Do I Need to Validate Before Buying a Cobot Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Validate the area for the robot, the infeed pick point, one or more pallet positions and operator access to remove full pallets. Then confirm reach: the robot must place the farthest case on the top layer of your tallest pallet. Pallet height and case size change the answer, so TRF validates reach, end-of-arm tool and pallet pattern for each application.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. The calculator on this page applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today, and returns an initial estimate that a TRF Sales Engineer completes with the costs of your project.

mainEntity.name: What Maintenance Does a Robotic Palletizer Require to Avoid Downtime?

acceptedAnswer.text: A robotic palletizer needs periodic inspection of the gripper, sensors and the robot itself, following the manufacturer's schedule. For TRF-supplied equipment, Parts and Service covers technical support, spare parts kept in the United States and the TRFCare preventive maintenance program.
